html: The Garrochambas were a small people of the highlands of southern Ecuador, in today's Loja province near the border with Peru. They are known mainly from Spanish reports of the 1500s, which list them among the peoples of the region with the Paltas and Calvas. The Inca conquered the area in the late 1400s. Under Spanish rule the Garrochambas merged into the mixed population of Ecuador, and their language and customs are almost unknown.
